stemBlocks.value: The temperature K of a liquid t minutes after heating is: t = 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 with K = 84, 61, 40, 29, 27, 26, 25 °C. (i) Using 2 cm to represent 10 minutes horizontally and 2 cm to represent 10 °C vertically, construct a temperature–time graph over the 60-minute interval. (ii) Draw a smooth curve through all the plotted points. (iii) Use the graph to estimate a) the temperature after 15 minutes, b) the rate of cooling at t = 30 minutes.
Think first: The temperature drops fast at first and then levels off, so the graph is a curve, not a straight line — and its steepness at a point is the rate of cooling there.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p235-q06 from workbook page 235.

solutionSteps.instruction: Set up the axes on the stated scales.

contentBlocks.value: Horizontal: 2 cm = 10 minutes, so mark 0 to 60. Vertical: 2 cm = 10 °C, so mark 0 to at least 90
Result: axes t from 0 to 60 min, K from 0 to 90 °C

solutionSteps.instruction: Plot the seven points from the table.
Join the points with one smooth curve, not a series of straight segments.

contentBlocks.value: The curve falls steeply at first and then flattens towards about 25 °C

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the curve at t = 15 minutes.

contentBlocks.value: t = 15 lies midway between the points (10, 61) and (20, 40); the curve there sits just below the midpoint 50.5

solutionSteps.instruction: Draw a tangent to the curve at t = 30 and take its gradient.

contentBlocks.value: Using a tangent through roughly (20, 40) and (40, 27): gradient = (27 − 40) ÷ (40 − 20) = −13 ÷ 20

solutionSteps.instruction: State the rate of cooling as a positive rate of decrease.

contentBlocks.value: The negative gradient means temperature is falling
Result: cooling at about 0.65 °C per minute

strategyBlocks.value: Plot the seven points on the given scales, join them with a smooth curve, read the temperature at t = 15 directly off the curve, then draw a tangent at t = 30 and find its gradient.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) and (ii) Plot (0, 84), (10, 61), (20, 40), (30, 29), (40, 27), (50, 26), (60, 25) on the given scales and join them with a smooth falling curve.  (iii) a) about 50 °C (accept 49–51 °C)  b) about 0.65 °C per minute (accept roughly 0.6–0.7 °C/min), i.e. the temperature is falling at that rate.

whyThisWorks.value: A cooling liquid loses heat fastest when it is hottest, so equal time steps produce ever-smaller temperature drops and the graph must curve. Because the curve is smooth, values between plotted points can be read off directly. The instantaneous rate of change at a single instant is not the gradient of a chord but the gradient of the tangent at that point, which is why part (b) needs a tangent drawn at t = 30.
